rows.goal: Sleep a chosen number of hours, from now or from a later bedtime | The Sleep dialog (src/ui/shell/TimeControls.tsx SleepDialog, run('life.sleep', { hours }) at :175; it never sends startAt) sends life.sleep. The command refuses: hours that aren't a number ('Say how long to sleep.', life.ts:368); a start that isn't finite (:371), is in the past, or is more than a day ahead (:373); and a start inside a kept commitment, through occupiedAt (:374, 'You’re at X until Y.'). It clamps hours to [SHORTEST_SLEEP, 16], stamps lastSleptAt as the wake when the night is booked, advances to the start, reads sleepQuality (nightParts: stress, the sleepQuality knob, a late hour), sets awakeSince to the wake, and advances to the wake while the world runs. Then applySleep moves energy, sleepDebt, stress, condition, morale and nourishment, and wokeWithDebt is set (:409). If requiresPlayer items fall inside the night it posts 'You Slept Through N Commitment(s)' (:414-423). Downstream: a commitment slept through is missed (the PLAN_KIND asleep branch; school classes and sessions through present(); appointments through presentForCare; rehearsals and coursework through awakeSince); sleepAlone gives no second night; readiness feeds focusOf; the waking drain reads wokeWithDebt.

rows.goal: Work Out from the Look After menu. Refused: in hospital; at energy < 25 ('too tired'); when injured (trainingRefusal); with the flu; during a kept commitment; on a clash within its 60 minutes; for a repeated actionId. Once the hour is lived, trainingAt (read as the hour ends) chooses run (1.1) or indoors (1). A second workout the same day builds 0.5^repeats. Fitness rises by workoutBuilds*builds, up to the age's ceiling. Energy falls by workoutCosts, nourishment by 6, hygiene by 20*hygieneDrift, stress by 8*stressRecovery; morale rises by 3*swing. The workout records stamina development and development.workout.at, adds to body.extra (exerts), and rolls an injury (mayHurt), which can bring a bill. Downstream: settleTheBody holds fitness three days; mendsTo turns fitness into condition; stamina feeds a task's consistency; trainingRefusal reads the injury; the health bill.

rows.goal: Put money away for a term, choose what happens at its end, break it, or take its interest | Breaks a term deposit before its end, at breakQuote's price. The penalty is days of interest by band, capped at the interest earned where the bank caps it, at least a week's interest in the first week, MUFG's early rate, or the interest forfeited as SLATE's estimate. It is free in a grace window or a cooling-off period, and refused where the bank doesn't allow breaking. breakTerm pays principal − (penalty beyond the interest) + kept interest − tax, closes the term and posts an Early Withdrawal Penalty expense. At NatWest it sets breakAt instead, and account_life closes the term when the 35 days' notice runs.

rows.goal: Move money between your own accounts, and open or close a savings account | Move Money moves an amount between two of the holder's own current or easy-access savings accounts. It's refused past the balance, for the same account, from an account a switch left in debt, when dormant, past Germany's allowance, past room after the withdrawal fee, or when closing. At one bank it posts at once; between banks it goes out now and lands in the sending bank's days, held to its limits. Past the free withdrawals it charges the fee. It counts as a withdrawal, and its balance effect feeds the fee waivers (lowest/average) and the no-withdrawals bonus.

rows.goal: Lock a card, report it lost or stolen, dispute a charge, and move to a new account number | Report It As Not Mine, on a stranger's use the holder has learned of and within the law's days from the statement, records reportedAt. It sets carried = liabilityFor from the use's own clocks (US debit: $50 within 2 business days of learning, $500 within 60 days of the statement, else all of it; credit: $50; a debit taken with the number alone: 0). It schedules bank.fraud_refund in the law's business days and stops and replaces the card free (not for a number-only debit). It's refused when already reported or past the window. The refund posts amount minus carried.

rows.goal: Open a current account at another bank, make it primary, move wages, standing orders, card autopay and a loan’s repayments to it, and close the old one | A current account opens at another bank where you live, either at once or after the bank's review. The application is refused if you already keep an account there or one is under review, if you owe that bank a charged-off debt, if a ChexSystems report turns you away, without a photo ID in force, under the bank's minimum age, at Capital One or Citi for anyone not a US person, or in a branch you can't get to. Opened accounts start at nothing; the opening deposit is sent in the sending bank's days; the debit card arrives in the bank's days. A refused application sends the deposit back, and an account left unfunded past the bank's days is closed.

rows.goal: Claim unemployment, apply for assistance, and register for Canada’s EI | Papers > Benefits > AssistancePanel 'Apply' runs benefits.assistance. assistanceRefusal checks: a scheme where they live; no open claim; SNAP only for a US citizen; provincial schemes only for a Canadian; age 18 or over; for SNAP, the student rule (in the summer without 87 hours a month); the Ontario and BC asset limits. It sets person.assistance and schedules ASSISTANCE_KIND (SNAP at +7 days). Each month the claim closes if they moved. SNAP's ABAWD limit allows 3 months in 36 without 80 hours, with an enrolled student exempt. A student without an exemption has the case closed with a 'Your SNAP Case Closed' notice. The amount is snapMonth on snapIncome (earned and unearned, work-study out), posted to an EBT escrow account with a 'SNAP Paid' notice. buyTheDaysFood draws on the EBT first.

rows.goal: Claim unemployment, apply for assistance, and register for Canada’s EI | Papers > Benefits 'File A Claim' runs benefits.claim. The button is hidden while studying, without permission to work, or with a short base period. Britain, Ireland and Mexico City route to their own claims. In the US the state is the base-period wages' state, or else the home state. The claim is refused when one is open, for a CT full-time student (CGS 31-235(b)), and for a non-citizen without a US work permit (FUTA). The monetary test runs on the basic or alternate base period. The command records the claim (CT has no waiting week) and schedules BENEFIT_WEEK_KIND for the next Sunday at 8 PM. Each week checks availability, reduces the benefit by the week's work (workedBetween -> weekBenefit), applies the waiting week, posts to the payee account and records the benefit through recordBenefit (yearOf().unemployment, the unearned kind). The claim closes at maxTotal or after a year. The return counts it as income.

rows.goal: Fired 30 days apart after benefits.assistance (SNAP's first a week on). It reads the scheme where they live, last month's income as snapIncome splits it (wages earned, interest and benefits unearned, work-study left out), the month's hours (workedBetween) and the ABAWD months counted. SNAP: an enrolled student is exempt from the time limit; a non-enrolled adult aged 18 to 64 with under 80 hours gets 'SNAP Time Limit Reached' after 3 counted months in 36; a student in the summer without 87 hours gets 'Your SNAP Case Closed' and closedAt; otherwise snapMonth is paid onto an EBT escrow account (opened at the first payment), claim.months rises, and 'SNAP Paid' is sent. Ontario Works and BC pay into the payee account. Moving away closes the claim. Downstream: the day's groceries draw on the EBT first.

rows.goal: Each Sunday at 20:00 after benefits.claim, the claim's week is certified. It reads the claim (weekly, maxTotal, paid, waited), whether they're available (in the US, studentUnavailable, work authorization, not in hospital or laid up), and the week's hours and pay (workedBetween → weekBenefit). The first week due is the unpaid waiting week, except in Connecticut. After that each week is posted to the payee account as 'Unemployment insurance', recordBenefit adds it to the year's unemployment and the month's unearned income, and claim.paid rises. The claim closes after a year or at maxTotal. Downstream: the year's tax return.

rows.goal: SHIFT_KIND (booked by planWeek for Saturdays or by take_shift for evenings). Absent: missed, the elective's hours freed, a notice.

rows.goal: Each School/Rep call cast() books (rehearsal, performance, understudy run-through, night on call) fires on the clock. Off sick or on the day called in sick: excused (a rehearsal's stage still a gap via callMissed; an excused last performance still closes the run). Otherwise tally.calls/answered; a rehearsal answered moves the process (callAnswered, a craft note at a work-through) and grows craft (rehearse); a performance played counts performed, nerves, friends' morale, is judged by reckonNight as the craft stood (band, work record, delivery, noteRun, listening, genres, nights, the night together's mood where classmates are cast, presence on a remarkable night, material) and then grows craft (playNight); the last night closes the run (closeRun: 'run' milestone, the director's note naming what held the nights back, reflect). Missed unexcused: rehearsal -> callMissed + missedCallsOut (castable false); performance -> noteRun 'missed', breach, and closeRun on the last. Downstream: evaluate (attendance, work nights, breaches), cast()/readRuns lastWork.delivery, the casting pool.

It leaves school.leave pending and schedules LEAVE_DECIDE_KIND for five working days, or for the next term's start if that comes first. rows.goal: Pay what’s owed on the Yale account, ask the aid office to review support past six terms, and convert work-study hours to grant aid | School, Shifts And Pay: Ask For Conversion To Grant Aid (StudyPlanPanels.tsx:296) runs school.request_conversion. It is refused unless the student is at school, has need-based aid, is not on leave, has no request already pending, and has convertible hours (assigned hours excused ill or hurt, or, once the spring is under way, hours never assigned). rows.reads: src/engine/systems/material.ts
rows.decisions: chooses: assignmentId, pace, scale, structure, prep, kept
rows.validation: refusals: — (also playingRefusal) | Time: None to choose; it’s rehearsed in by the steps of rehearsal and the rehearsals kept with your partner; Money: None; A Change Of Mind: Keeps 50% of what was rehearsed in (an estimate) | costs: Each side leans the work toward the abilities it draws on and adds no weight. Work on the feet rehearses the choice in, and a change of mind keeps half of what was rehearsed in. The showing or the night reads the work as it’s played. No time passes and no money moves
rows.changes: “Chosen: rehearsed in to …%.” A first choice starts at 0%; the same choice again keeps all of it; a different one keeps 50%.; Leaving every axis open takes the choice away.; The sides chosen are kept on your record of how you play.
rows.later: Each step of rehearsal rehearses it in by 90% of that step’s own share, of what’s left, and keeps doing so after its own part is complete, until the choice reaches 90%. A rehearsal kept with your partner does the same, by 90% of its own share.; The showing reads it with the rest of the preparation, and Your Work So Far names a side you choose most of the time as a habit.
rows.systems: Rehearsing With A Partner, scheduled: A rehearsal kept with your partner rehearses the choice in too, as a step of rehearsal does.; Feedback And Your Notes, evaluation: The showing reads the choice: its lean, the abilities it draws on, and how far it’s rehearsed in.; Your Work So Far, history: Every side chosen and shown is kept, and Your Work So Far names one you choose most of the time. | the evaluation’s lean and misfit at a showing and a night (systems/material.ts, systems/evaluation.ts); rehearseChoice, which a rehearsal on the feet and a call read (systems/material.ts); noteMaterial, the approaches tried (systems/experience.ts)
rows.sees: Fully Prepared is the expected result with no draw, every part complete and a good day: what the choice can reach, not where the work stands now.; “Doesn’t fit:” under a side says the scene doesn’t take it, and why.; “Your choice now is rehearsed in to …% (complete at 90%)” is how far along it is.; With nothing chosen, the work is read by its own genre and material alone. | assignment; school
rows.saveLoad: Your Work So Far: Every side chosen and shown is kept, and Your Work So Far names one you choose most of the time. | the assignment’s playing (its sides, chosenAt, prep); the casting process’s playing
rows.failure: refusals said in the player's words: — (also playingRefusal) | Until 2026-10-12 this was called Verified on tests/trace-commands.test.ts alone, whose title said the showing read the choice while the test checked only that a shown scene refused a new one. What’s driven through the engine there: school.choose_playing chooses a way, work on the feet (school.prepare) rehearses it in, and a change keeps half of it (PLAYING.keptOnChange); school.choose_part_playing is refused before you’re cast, chosen once you are, and rehearsed in at the calls. What isn’t: that the showing reads the way is checked on its forecast (forecastWork, built on the same workContext as the showing’s judgeWork) against the same work with the way taken off by hand, and no showing is run; no test checks that a night reads a part’s way; a shown scene’s refusal is checked on a status set by hand; and that each side leans the work and adds no weight is checked at function level, on materialContext and evaluate (tests/material.test.ts). A new play has no material profile, so its scene or part offers no choice. No test reloads a save with a choice rehearsed in

rows.preconditions: A piece in progress: a scene for class with its material, still open; a practice brief with a reading chosen; a part whose run is still to come.; Some of the lines learned first: 30% of a brief’s, a scene’s or a part’s.; A problem named before a way is tried, and any change tried kept or put back before the next.; For a way on your feet, energy of 25 or more and no injury that stops training. For any, awake, out of hospital, at nothing else, and free for its minutes.; Preparing Coursework first: A scene’s lines learned to 30% let you try a way at it, and a problem in a part of the preparation is answered by that part’s own step. | A piece in progress with a problem its forecast shows (problemsOf); a reading chosen and lines learned for an adjustment on the feet; awake, not too spent or hurt; nothing waiting to be kept or put back before another try, and something waiting before it’s settled | refused where: — (also identifyRefusal)
rows.reads: src/engine/systems/workbook.ts
rows.decisions: chooses: piece, problem, label, measure
rows.validation: refusals: — (also identifyRefusal) | Time: Work It Slowly, 30 minutes; Run Into It From The One Before, 40 minutes; Play This Part Another Way, 30 minutes; Find Places To Breathe, 45 minutes; Name What You Want In Each Part, 30 minutes; Run It With Your Partner, 45 minutes (an estimate); Money: None; Naming And Settling: No time: naming a problem, keeping a change and putting one back move no clock | costs: Naming a problem keeps it as the one being worked. A try spends its time on an adjustment the problem admits, and keeps the problem’s figure in the forecast before and after. A change of how a beat is played is kept, and every later forecast and performance reads it, or put back and not offered for that problem again. Nothing is drawn: the same work tried the same way shows the same evidence
rows.changes: Naming a problem keeps it as the one being worked on.; A way tried spends its minutes and changes the work, and the try is kept with its figure before and after.; Work done (working a part slowly, running into it, naming what you want, running it with a reader) is kept at once, and a problem it solves leaves the list by itself.; Playing a part another way, or finding places to breathe, waits on Keep It or Put It Back. Kept, it’s a discovery. Put back, the piece is as it was, and that way isn’t offered for the problem again.; Working on an ability’s problem trains it a little, and running into a part trains your adaptability.
rows.later: Every later forecast and performance of the piece reads what was kept: the take of a brief, the showing of a scene, a night of a part.; What You’ve Found lists each part played its own way and how far it’s rehearsed in, places to breathe found, and each try kept that moved its figure half a point or more.
rows.systems: Feedback And Your Notes, evaluation: The showing reads the scene with each part’s own work and every discovery kept.; Preparing A Brief, evaluation: A brief’s take reads its beats’ own work and the ways kept, as its forecast did.; Who Reads With You, immediate: Run It With Your Partner moves the preparation of a classmate reading a brief with you.; The Player Profile, immediate: Working on an ability’s problem trains it a little, and running into a part trains adaptability. | withBook, which every take, showing and night reads (systems/piece.ts); problemsOf and optionsOf (systems/workbook.ts); each piece’s forecast (systems/workpieces.ts)
rows.sees: Before and after are the problem’s own figure: a part’s result for a problem in one part, the last part’s for tiring late, the whole for an ability or a part of the preparation, the work together for a partner.; A try that barely moves its figure is evidence too: the problem may want another way, or its own step of preparation.; “No way at it is left here” means its own step of preparation answers it, or the ways tried were put back. A partner not there yet on a scene for class has none here either: its line ends “Ask … to rehearse it with you.”; The tries table keeps the last six, newest first, each Kept, Put back or Waiting. | work; assignment
rows.saveLoad: (none) | the piece’s workbook (problem, tries, discoveries) and its segments’ work: Person.briefs[id].book, the assignment’s book, the casting process’s book
rows.failure: refusals said in the player's words: — (also identifyRefusal) | Until 2026-10-12 this was called Verified, while no test played a night after a way was kept, and these limits said no test worked a class scene, while tests/defects-g8-9.test.ts did. Driven through the commands and checked on a brief: a problem named, an adjustment tried and its evidence kept, a change of a beat waiting to be kept or put back, put back and not offered for that problem again, and kept, read by the forecast and by the next take, a self-tape (tests/workbook.test.ts). On a class scene (assignment:<id>) a problem is named and an adjustment tried, its figure rising (tests/defects-g8-9.test.ts), and nothing is kept or put back there, or shown after. On a part, tests/direction.test.ts keeps the ways the director’s notes lead to through work.settle and plays to the last rehearsal call, checking the notes, and no test plays a night after a way is kept. So withBook is checked through a take alone: a showing and a night read the same book (systems/coursework.ts, playPiece in systems/school.ts), and no test checks either after a way is kept

rows.goal: A bank closing an idle German account at zero (closedByBank and the dormancy/idle path): it can go negative from fees on closing; make the bank's own close settle consistently; closure can't erase debt or strand money; closed accounts stop all recurring processing.
rows.entry: systems/bankmoves.ts closedByBank, closeNow, closeRefusal; systems/lending.ts closeForOverdraft, completeSwitch; systems/banking.ts settleFees, closingFeesOf, dropPaymentsFor; systems/abroad.ts homeCloses; systems/accountlife.ts cancelRefusal, bank.cancel_new; systems/routing.ts redirectAway; content/guide/money.ts bank.other-banks, bank.borrowing, bank.upkeep; content/tutorial.ts the bank chapter's overdraft sentence
rows.preconditions: BGB § 675h(2): a payment service provider ends a framework contract on at least two months' notice; § 675h(3): on termination, regularly charged fees are owed pro rata up to the end of the contract (dejure.org text, read 2026-10-16; gesetze-im-internet.de refused the fetch with 503). So fees accrued to the closing are owed, not forgiven, and a balance can't be manufactured where there is none to take them from. The project's own rule (CLAUDE.md, the ledger law; brief section 7): every movement a balanced posting, funds never vanish or duplicate, a closure can't strand money or erase a debt. SLATE's existing rule for a customer's close (bankmoves.ts closeRefusal:282-307, accountlife.ts cancelRefusal:237-261): the bank closes an overdrawn account only once that's paid.
rows.reads: No German bank reaches the bank's own close at zero: closedByBank (bankmoves.ts:333-340) runs only from the day's check at bankmoves.ts:420-438, which reads OPENING (content/bankopening.ts:44-84), and only Citi (closesAtZeroAfterDays 90) and Capital One (fundWithinDays 60) carry those rules. Germany has no unclaimed-money law (content/accountlife.ts UNCLAIMED.DE has no years), so idleAccounts (accountlife.ts:609-646) never closes a German account, and dormancy (accountlife.ts:616-619) blocks without closing. So the defect named is latent: closedByBank checks `balance !== 0` before closeNow (bankmoves.ts:310-326), which then settles interest (settleInterest, banking.ts:508) and fees (settleFees, banking.ts:492-500, Germany's quarter only); with no remainderTo, interest settled would stay on a closed account (stranded), and fees would leave a closed account negative with nothing pursuing it (leftOverdrawn, lending.ts:937-953, skips closed accounts). Reproduced only with a bank given a zero-close rule in a test (TEST SETUP). The German bank's own close that does happen is the overdraft's (closeForOverdraft, lending.ts:955-1054): reproduced on a Berlin quickSave (probe, Commerzbank primary, a Deutsche Bank AktivKonto €100 under from 5 January 2026): charged off on 7 March at €101.97 with feesDue €13.80 (January's and February's €6.90) left on the closed account and never charged, and March's fee and the overdraft interest built since 1 March (odAccrued) dropped too. Played the same way at a home account abroad (a German home bank's AktivKonto emptied to Chase, its €6.90 overdrawing it).
rows.decisions: closedByBank: work out what closing would settle (interest net of tax, the fees closing charges, the overdraft interest built) before closing; close only where that leaves nothing owed, and send anything it leaves (interest) to the current account kept elsewhere by the bank's own payment, never stranded; where closing would leave it owing, don't close: the charges post at their regular closing and the account is pursued as any overdrawn one (the 60 days, closeForOverdraft), as the customer's Close It refuses it. closeForOverdraft: settle the overdraft interest built and, on each account it closes, Germany's quarter of fees before the set-off, so they're set off or charged off with the rest, never dropped; the quiet re-banking after a charge-off doesn't settle them a second time or move a negative to the new bank. Scheduled payments and standing orders into an account it closes dropped (dropPaymentsFor), as every other close does. Recurring processing on a closed account checked one by one (interest, fees, the abroad fee, statements, round-ups, alerts, standing orders) and tested.
rows.validation: closedByBank's settlement: necessary defensive guard (no current journey gives it anything to settle). closeForOverdraft's dropped fees and overdraft interest: required reachable behavior (a played home account abroad reaches it).

rows.goal: Found on the way (2026-10-16, before any change): overdraft interest built in the month is dropped by every close, so a closure erases that debt.
rows.entry: systems/banking.ts (a settling function beside settleFees); systems/bankmoves.ts closeNow, closeRefusal; systems/accountlife.ts bank.cancel_new, cancelRefusal; systems/abroad.ts homeCloses; systems/lending.ts completeSwitch, closeForOverdraft; content/guide/money.ts
rows.preconditions: As banking.1: closure can't erase a debt (the brief's section 7; CLAUDE.md's ledger law). Interest on an overdraft accrues day by day and is owed to the day the account ends; the bank charges it on the first (lending.ts:1101-1110), and the overdraft panel says “it’s charged on the first” (ui/bank/BankLending.tsx:213-214).
rows.reads: odAccrued builds nightly on an overdrawn current account (lending.ts:1066-1100) and is charged only on the 1st (lending.ts:1101-1110). No closing path reads it: closeNow (bankmoves.ts:310-326), bank.cancel_new (accountlife.ts:517-577), homeCloses (abroad.ts:501-551), completeSwitch's open() (lending.ts:715-746) and closeForOverdraft (lending.ts:955-1054) close the account with it unsettled, and nothing charges a closed account. US banks charge overdrafts by the item (no rate), so a New Haven account builds none; every bank a home account abroad can be kept at except NZ's BNZ and Japan's MUFG builds it (LENDING overdraft rates, read by probe). Played: a home account abroad overdrawn by its fees, paid back from Chase, then Close It before the 1st; or Barclays' own close on its notice after the account was overdrawn that month. Close It's refusal (closeRefusal) and Cancel It's (cancelRefusal) don't count it, so a close could also leave the account below zero once it is charged.
rows.decisions: A settling step that charges the overdraft interest built (whole cents, the fraction dropped as the 1st drops it), against the Overdraft Interest line, called in every closing path before the account closes; Close It's and Cancel It's refusals count it with the fees, in the bank's words; Canada's and Mexico's refund leaves it out, as it leaves out overdraft interest already (chargesBackOf).

rows.goal: Found on the way: a standing order from an account the bank closed on its own fails every month for good, and says so every month.

rows.preconditions: A standing order is an instruction the paying bank holds; when that bank closes the account, the order has nowhere to run from. The brief's section 9 (no repeated event execution) and 11 (identical feedback not repeated without regard to state); banking.md item 1: closed accounts stop all recurring processing, standing orders and alerts among them.
rows.reads: bank.close_current refuses while an order pays from the account (closeRefusal, bankmoves.ts:290-291, linkedTo routing.ts:83-113), but a bank's own close doesn't ask: closedByBank (bankmoves.ts:333-340) and closeForOverdraft (lending.ts:997-1046) leave orders from it in place (redirectAway, routing.ts:122-129, says they “fail, and say so”), so payments.ts:198-219 posts “A Standing Order Didn’t Go … is closed” each month for good. closeForOverdraft doesn't call dropPaymentsFor (banking.ts:475-485) either, so orders into a savings account it closed fail monthly the same way. Played: a New Haven student whose order pays from a Capital One account closed unfunded.
rows.decisions: On a bank's own close, the orders paying from the account end with it, and the closing notice says which, once; orders into it and payments set for a date go as dropPaymentsFor takes them on every other close.

rows.entry: systems/banking.ts settleFees, closingFeesOf; every closing path that calls them; four existing tests whose titles the audit cites
rows.preconditions: BGB § 675h(3): “Im Fall der Kündigung sind regelmäßig erhobene Entgelte nur anteilig …” (dejure.org, read 2026-10-16): on termination a monthly account fee is owed pro rata to the end.
rows.reads: closingFeesOf (banking.ts:503-505) and settleFees (banking.ts:492-500) charge the quarter so far plus the whole of this month's fee (feeFor at the month's start), whatever day of the month the account closes. tests/scope-money.test.ts's Berlin Close It and Cancel It (a Commerzbank GiroKonto opened and closed on 5 January, “refused … for its €4.90 month”) and tests/accountlife.test.ts's two German quarter tests assert the whole month, and their titles are cited by the audit (docs/verification/audit/money.json).
rows.decisions: Record it, with the rule and the uncertainty (how a German bank counts the share: by days open in the month, from the opening day where it opened that month, SLATE's reading), and leave the decision to the owner: charging pro rata falsifies three cited test titles, which the instructions forbid renaming and the audit's pipeline inputs cite.

rows.goal: Interest withdrawn from a term deposit before 2026-10-15 (Take Interest) isn't found when the term is canceled in its cooling-off period.
rows.entry: systems/accountlife.ts interestPaidSince, a migration beside it; core/ledger.ts Account (one optional field); src/engine/index.ts ONCE_ON_OPENING and loadSave; content/guide/money.ts bank.upkeep or bank.term
rows.preconditions: Where the country's rule returns what each side received on a withdrawal (Directive 2002/65/EC art. 7(4)-(5); BGB § 355(3); Mexico's LTOSF art. 11 Bis 1, as cited in accountlife.ts:131-157), interest already paid out of the term goes back on canceling it, with its tax, and off the year's income. The project's rules: never fabricate a transaction or double-count income; an older save keeps its legitimate balances and history; a one-time step on opening is named in SaveUniverse.opened so a reload never repeats it (index.ts:279-286, 327-334, followTheCover).
rows.reads: Since a4d05745 (2026-10-15) bank.take_term_interest posts a zero posting against the term (accountlife.ts:484-501) and interestPaidSince (accountlife.ts:176-179) finds a term's taken interest by it. A build before that (git show a4d05745^:src/engine/systems/accountlife.ts:294-309) posted only the primary account (net), the Interest income line (gross) and Tax On Interest, memo “Interest: <term name>”, a name every term at the bank shares. So in an older save interestBackOf (accountlife.ts:192-199) finds nothing: cancelRefusal doesn't count it and bank.cancel_new (accountlife.ts:549-557) returns none of it; the interest stays paid and on the year's income. Reproduced by writing a save as that build wrote it (the zero posting taken off, `opened` without the new step) and canceling. The records an older save holds that tell same-named terms apart: the term's own id, opening instant, fixed rate, balance and accrued (what's left built after each take, accountlife.ts:498), and the clock's day ends (life.ts:350-358): the interest a term builds is its balance × rate / 365 at each day's end (lending.ts:1162), so each take was the whole cents of what it had built since opening less what was taken before, and what's left is term.accrued. A transaction's memo, date, gross, net and the account it went into are kept; nothing else names the term.
rows.decisions: A one-time step on opening (`findTermInterest`, named in SaveUniverse.opened): for each open term deposit still in its cooling-off, its bank letting interest be taken during the term, the untagged “Interest: <name>” transactions into its holder's account from its opening on are the candidates; the term's own accrual is replayed day end by day end from its opening (its balance × its rate / 365, each candidate taken where it equals the whole cents built then), and only a set of candidates that reproduces the term's stored accrued exactly is taken as its own, the earliest where two fit, and none taken by another term. Recorded on the term as the transactions' ids; interestPaidSince reads them beside the tag. Where no set fits, nothing is attributed: the interest stays as the build that paid it left it (that build never returned it), never taken back from a term that may not have paid it. The guide says what it does.

rows.goal: `repriceCare`'s insurer portion (planPaid, near health.ts:1530) doesn't match its documented intent: find exactly how, decide what's right, fix, and prove consistent totals, no double charge, no duplicated payment, and that a coverage change never silently rewrites a bill already issued or paid
rows.entry: health.repriceCare; health.careFor (care log's plan part); MedicalBill (adjustment lines); Papers Care And Its Bills (Your Share, Due, Plan Paid); medical debt account; school.withdraw, school.buy_affiliate and the leave's cover canceled back (callers); guide papers.health-cover
rows.preconditions: THE PROJECT'S OWN RULES: repriceCare's comment (health.ts:1508-1513): 'More owed is a new bill, said for what it is; less comes off the bill still open, and what's left of it back to the bank. Every change is a posting or a bill of its own: nothing already on a statement is rewritten'; and at 1530: 'What the plan paid of the bill follows: nothing where the cover now reads none'. The house standard: 'A ledger balance is never a number somebody typed. It is the sum of postings.' The owner's brief §9 (no duplicate processing, no contradictory statuses) and this pass's item: patient + insurer = price; never double-charges; never duplicates a payment; historical bills stand; say what repricing may change and when. The plan rules: a care's price to a plan is planPrice (CARE.price grown by the medical price index); a plan pays price − share where it pays (careFor, health.ts:1479-1482): not for a Yale Health member's visit outside its Health Center (outsideItsPractice), not for restricted scope's non-hospital care, nothing while a claim stands denied.
rows.reads: health.ts:1514-1546. Reproduced on a fixture (probe/health/reprice.ts, run 2026-10-16, git-ignored): (a) a Yale Health emergency on 2 September 2026, its bill m1 $50.00 with covered {price $3,323.84, planPaid $3,273.84}, repriced as uninsured (cover canceled back to 1 August): Connecticut's charity takes the uninsured price to $0 for that income, so m1 is rewritten in place to amount $0.00, paid: true (Papers says Settled for a bill nobody paid), planPaid $0.00, with no word on the bill of the charity or the change; the issued bill's figures are gone (1530-1532, 1541). (b) An uninsured emergency on 10 September (no bill: charity free), then covered back by Yale Health: a new bill m2 of $50.00 with no plan part at all: the plan's $3,273.84 is written nowhere, so patient + insurer = $50.00 against a $3,323.84 price (1532 runs only where the bill already had `covered`). (c) The plan part is set from `planOf` (a plan exists) rather than whether the plan pays this care (outside its practice, restricted scope, a standing denial), and is skipped altogether when the share is unchanged (1527 continues before 1532). (d) Found on the way: a credit on care whose bill went to medical debt is refunded to the bank (1540-1542, `open` excludes inDebt) while the debt for the same care stands: paid twice over, once in cash and once owed.
rows.decisions: Decided: a bill as issued stands. repriceCare never writes an existing bill's plan part, and never changes a bill paid or in debt. Each care event it changes gets one adjustment line of its own (a MedicalBill naming the bill it adjusts): more owed is billed on it and due in 30 days, as now; less owed is its credit, which comes off the open original's balance first (recorded on the original as `credited`, so its issued share stays readable and Papers says Credited), then off the medical debt where the original went to debt, then back to the bank. The plan's part follows the cover now: what the plan pays now (price − share where a plan pays this care now, 0 where none does) less what the lines already show for it, written on the adjustment line as the plan's change (negative where the plan takes back). The care log keeps each event's plan part. So for every care, the patient's lines (issued less credited and credits) sum to its share now, and the plan's lines sum to the plan's part now: patient + insurer = the price where the cover pays it. Uninsured hospital care repriced with Connecticut's charity says so on its line. Papers draws an adjustment's credit and the plan's change.

rows.preconditions: ENACTED: Covered Connecticut is for an adult 19–64 with household income to 175% of the poverty line who is "ineligible for HUSKY Health/Medicaid due to income", "eligible for financial help" (APTC and CSRs), using 100% of it, in a silver plan (portal.ct.gov/dss/health-and-home-care/covered-connecticut-program, read 2026-10-16); Access Health CT: "don't qualify for Medicaid due to income" and "If your household income makes you eligible for HUSKY Health/Medicaid, you are not eligible for the Covered CT Program" (help.accesshealthct.com/en_US/covered-connecticut-program, read 2026-10-16, 'Income Guidelines for 2026 Coverage'); the OHS eligibility summary of 8 July 2021 defined it as an income band above HUSKY's limit ("greater than 160%, and up to and including 175%" for parents). FEDERAL AUTHORITY: CMS's approval of 15 December 2022 (demonstration 11-W-00402/1, to 31 December 2027) authorizes expenditure for adults "who are not Medicaid eligible" to 175% and eligible for APTC, and describes them as having "income that is above the Medicaid limit" (medicaid.gov covered-ct-ca.pdf, read 2026-10-16). THE CREDIT: in 2026 a lawfully present noncitizen at 100–400% who is not eligible for other minimum essential coverage is an applicable taxpayer (26 USC 36B(c)(1)(A); 26 CFR 1.36B-2(b)(1)); the under-100% exception for the lawfully present barred by status (36B(c)(1)(B), 1.36B-2(b)(5)) was struck for taxable years after 2025 (Pub. L. 119-21 §71302); from 2027 only an "eligible alien" (green card, Cuban/Haitian entrant, COFA) has it (§71301; 45 CFR 155.305(f)(1)(ii)(C), 155.20, read 2026-10-16). UNCERTAINTY: no Access Health CT or DSS document read states how it treats a noncitizen barred from HUSKY D by status at 100–138%; the state's published words ("due to income"; "if your household income makes you eligible for HUSKY") are implemented, and the status-barred person is given the marketplace, whose credit the return gives from 100% (item 5).
rows.reads: health.ts:430-431 (programFor): Covered Connecticut is given to anybody lawfully present whose last month is ≤175% of the year before's line and for whom creditAllowed (≥100% and creditStatus) holds; it never asks whether the income is over HUSKY D's 138%. A noncitizen barred from HUSKY D by status (medicaidStatus false from 1 October 2026, health.ts:330-334; 418 skipped) at 100–138% is given Covered Connecticut. Reproduced by reading: an F-1 student in 2026 with a month of $1,500.00 (between $1,304.17 and $1,835.40) falls through 418 to 431 and gets {kind:'essential'}. The return (taxreturn.ts:1033) also reads ≤138% as 'a person Medicaid would take' whatever the status, so the marketplace's credit is none for that person (and none at all for a 1040-NR filer, taxreturn.ts:1035; item 5).
rows.decisions: programFor: Covered Connecticut only where last month's income is over HUSKY D's line (current year, 138%) and within 175% of the year before's, whatever the status: an income HUSKY D's line takes is not 'ineligible due to income'. The status-barred person at 100–138% falls to the marketplace (open enrollment or 60 days), with the credit on the return from 100% (taxreturn: the 138% exclusion applies only where the status admits Medicaid). Dated comment with the sources and the uncertainty. Guide and Papers sentences updated.

rows.decisions: A month is deemed to meet the work test where, for any part of it, she was under 19 or 65 or over (435.551/435.553(a)(1)), or received SNAP while not exempt from its work rules (435.554(c)(7)), or (on her request, 435.555(d)(1)) had an inpatient stay. The age and SNAP exceptions are read ex parte (435.557: reliable information available to the State); the stay is granted on the request the notice of noncompliance offers (item 3), through a new command `health.request_hardship`. Each applied before denial or termination. The unreadable ones recorded in a dated comment.

rows.entry: taxreturn.figuresFor (credit); health.creditStatus; Papers The Marketplace text; guide papers.health-cover
rows.preconditions: ENACTED (2026): an applicable taxpayer's household income at 100–400% (26 USC 36B(c)(1)(A)), filing jointly if married (36B(c)(1)(C)); a month of coverage counts only while lawfully present (36B(e)), which before §71301 took effect included nonimmigrant status (45 CFR 155.20 'lawfully present' (2): 'a valid nonimmigrant status, as defined in 8 U.S.C. 1101(a)(15)'; an F-1 is 1101(a)(15)(F)). Nothing excludes a nonresident alien: 26 CFR 1.36B-2(b) has no such rule (law.cornell.edu, read 2026-10-16); IRS Pub. 974 (2025): "You must file Form 8962 with your income tax return (Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR)" when taking the PTC; Instructions for Form 1040-NR (2025): exceptions only for dependents, for the spouse's advance payments, and for a married 1040-NR filer (irs.gov, read 2026-10-16). The marketplace: 45 CFR 155.305(a)(1) and (f)(1) (read 2026-10-16). FROM 2027: only an 'eligible alien' (36B(e)(2)(B) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 §71301, taxable years after 31 December 2026; 45 CFR 155.305(f)(1)(ii)(C)), which an F-1 student isn't. So in 2026 an unmarried F-1 student in status, not eligible for Yale Health or other minimum essential coverage, at 100–400%, qualifies for APTC and the PTC on Form 1040-NR; from 2027 she doesn't. SLATE's simulation: no advance payments are modeled; the whole premium is paid and the credit is taken on the return (health.ts header), and SLATE's lives are unmarried.
rows.reads: Covered Connecticut (which needs APTC eligibility) reads creditStatus, true for anybody lawfully present before 2027 (health.ts:357-360): right. But the return gives no credit to a nonresident alien at all (taxreturn.ts:1034-1035: 'A nonresident alien isn't an applicable taxpayer for the premium tax credit, which the 1040-NR doesn't carry'): false by Pub. 974 and the 1040-NR instructions, and contradictory with Covered Connecticut, which SLATE gives her in 2026 as eligible for that very credit. It also reads no status for 2027 (an F-1's premiums in 2027 would get the credit as a resident's would, were she not a nonresident). Reproduced by reading figuresFor: credit = 0 whenever nra.
rows.decisions: figuresFor: the credit for a 1040-NR filer as for any (unmarried, as every SLATE life is), read the status by creditStatus at the year's end (none for an F-1 from 2027), and the 138% exclusion only where Medicaid would take her by status (medicaidStatus at the year's end). Dated comment with the sources. Papers' line and the guide say an F-1 student has the credit in 2026 and none from 2027.

rows.goal: FOUND ON THE WAY: the work test's $580 a month is MAGI-based monthly income, not wages alone

rows.preconditions: REGULATION: 42 CFR 435.552(f): an applicable individual demonstrates community engagement for a month with "a monthly income that is not less than" the federal minimum wage × 80 ($580), and "(2) The agency must determine the monthly income based on the individual's MAGI-based income, for their MAGI-based household, as defined at § 435.603"; the preamble: "countable income under § 435.603(e) generally includes earned income as well as countable unearned income, meaning that States must take into account all of this income"; CMS "considered counting only earned income" and rejected it (CMS-2454-IFC, read 2026-10-16). CT: "Monthly income of at least $580/month" (CHA 8/25/26).
rows.reads: health.ts:594-603 (lastMonthWork) reads only the pay of wages (workedBetween, earnings.ts:207-219), and its comment says that from 2026-10-12 'a benefit, interest or a pension' no longer pass; Papers (PapersWorkspace.tsx:560: 'a benefit, interest or a pension isn’t work') and the guide (guide/papers.ts:263, 302) say the same. Reproduced: tests/need-paths.test.ts 'on Covered Connecticut ... her October 2027 is $930.00 ...' ends the twin with $930.00 of interest in October 2027 (and $2,052.00 a month before it) for having no work, where her income alone is the $580.
rows.decisions: A month meets the income criterion where the month's income on the record (earningsOf.months, the same income programFor reads: wages, work-study, unemployment, interest, pensions) plus any wages posted that the record doesn't hold reaches $580. Hours (80) and the School as now. Papers and guide sentences corrected. The need-paths test whose title says the $930.00 twin is told the work test is why: its claim falsified; renamed only by keeping its old title whole inside the new one ('until 2026-10-16: …'), so the audit's citation still lands, with the twin moved to income under $580.

rows.preconditions: The Permanent Incomplete and Fail notices offer the year’s end only where `repeatRefusal` would grant it (the project’s own rule since 2026-10-15, courserecord.ts:153-162); the count is the Bulletin’s nine semesters (Yale Bulletin, David Geffen School of Drama 2026–2027 (https://bulletin.yale.edu/sites/default/files/david-geffen-school-of-drama-2026-2027.pdf, PDF created 11 August 2026, read 2026-10-16), p.194: “students must complete the degree requirements within nine semesters”) under SLATE’s repeat (SLATE’s faculty model: the Bulletin has no rule for repeating). On a leave the Bulletin lets a student complete outstanding work in courses for which extensions have been granted (p.158, item 5).
rows.reads: school.ts:2950-2957: on a leave under way, next = firstTerm − (offset − (returnTerm − firstTerm)), the program term taken again on return; otherwise academicTerm(termsBegun − 1) + 1. Only INCOMPLETE_DUE_KIND reaches it on a leave (kept() keeps it, leave.ts:160; an evaluation is called off on a leave, so tellFails never runs on one). Reproduced 2026-10-16 (probe, seed rr-lv1): Acting I called in sick eleven times in Fall Term 2026 (TEST SETUP: the flu) leaves four Incompletes due Sunday 10 January 2027 at five; a medical leave asked Monday 14 December begins with Spring Term 2027 (4 January); each Incomplete extended once to Tuesday 9 February 2027 at five; on that day, on the leave, each becomes Permanent, its notice offering the year’s end; back for Spring Term 2028 and registered, at its evaluation of Friday 28 April 2028 `repeatRefusal` says nothing, and the repeat asked is granted for the four. Worked by hand: the branch counts 1 enrolled + the year’s 2 again + 4 after + (2 − 1) still to take = 8; without it next is academicTerm(1) + 1 = 0 and the count 9: both within nine. `leaveLengths` grants only two-term leaves while every year of the curriculum has year-long courses, so the branch counts 8 + 2 per repeat granted and the other path 9 + 2 per repeat: the same side of nine in every reachable state. It decides only for a three-term leave (count 8 against 10), which the Bulletin allows (p.158) and `leaveLengths` would grant for a curriculum of one-term courses.
rows.decisions: Play the preferred journey through the commands and the clock and assert the notices against `repeatRefusal` and the Standing tab at the year’s end; play a twin that makes the extended Incomplete up on the leave (p.158 item 5). Mutation-check the branch: removed, the played journey still passes (the branch decides nothing reachable, recorded); a GUARD test on a three-term leave (TEST SETUP: the leave’s length set to three before it begins, which `leaveLengths` refuses today) kills it. Keep the branch with a dated comment saying why.

rows.entry: src/engine/systems/taxreturn.ts (nextNotice, tax.file, armCollection, resumeCollection, endPlan, TAX_NOTICE_KIND handler); src/engine/content/guide/taxes.ts (taxes.return later, taxes.pay short and later, IRS_LEVY_DAYS); src/engine/content/tutorial.ts (the taxes sentence); src/ui/workspaces/PapersWorkspace.tsx (Returns fine print); tests/evidence-g17-papers.test.ts, tests/liens-and-arrangements.test.ts, tests/scope-taxpapers.test.ts (assertions that encode the from-filing count)
rows.preconditions: Tax shown on a return is due at the time fixed for filing it, without assessment or notice and demand (IRC 6151(a), read at law.cornell.edu 2026-10-16). Notice and demand follows an assessment, within 60 days of it (IRC 6303(a)); a levy is lawful only once the tax is unpaid 10 days after notice and demand (6331(a)) and after 30 days' written notice of intent (6331(d)(2)). Interest and the failure-to-pay penalty run only from the due date (6601(a), 6651(a)(2)). The IRS's published sequence is a first bill (CP14, 'If you owe taxes, we will send you a bill. This is your first bill for tax due'), at least one more bill, a final bill, then collection (IRS Publication 594, Rev. 1-2026, read 2026-10-16); the IRM puts the assessment (23C) date and the first notice date on the Monday of the third week after Master File posting (IRM 3.30.123.5.5, read 2026-10-16). So a balance-due bill (CP14) after processing is valid for a return filed early, naming the due date; a reminder that the balance is overdue (CP501 'you still owe it, with the interest and penalty since'), a second reminder (CP503), a notice of intent to levy (CP504) or a final notice (LT11) before the due date is premature. Whether the IRS holds an early return's CP14 until the due date wasn't found (uncertainty recorded). Connecticut: a tax 'due and unpaid' (Conn. Gen. Stat. 12-734) is collected on failure to pay 'within thirty days of its due date' (12-35(a)(2), (a)(3)), with notice 'not less than thirty days before the day the warrant is to be issued' for a bank account (12-35(b)(1)); read at codes.findlaw.com 2026-10-16.
rows.reads: Reproduced 2026-10-16 (probe/tax/repro-notice.ts, the Scraping family's played life, seed r3-tax-scraping): her 2027 return filed on Papers on 1 February 2028 with her money in a CD, $1,700.39 owed to the IRS, due 18 April 2028 at 11:59 PM. tax.file's unpaid branch (src/engine/systems/taxreturn.ts:1566) sets collection 0 and calls nextNotice (:389-393), which schedules from sim.now: CP501 on 7 March 2028 ('Notice CP501: $1,700.39 on your 2027 return; you still owe it, with the interest and penalty since.') and CP503 on 11 April, both before the due date, when no interest or penalty had run; CP504 on 16 May and LT11 on 20 June 2028, so the levy came 17 July, 90 days after the due date. No CP14 is ever sent: the first letter is a reminder. The same from-now count is in resumeCollection (:603-612, a plan refused before the due date) and endPlan (:631, a plan ended before it), and armCollection (:1165-1182) arms a save opened with a balance and no letter the same way; a save from before the fix holds its premature letter pending. Connecticut's side counts from max(now, its due date) since 2026-10-15 (statetax.ts:392-401): its bill came 18 May 2028, 30 days after the due date, and nothing before it.
rows.decisions: (1) nextNotice counts each step from the later of now and the return's due date, so no reminder, notice of intent or final notice precedes the due date, wherever collection is put on the calendar (filing, a plan refused or ended, a save opened). (2) tax.file sends the IRS's bill, Notice CP14, when it leaves a balance the bank couldn't pay and no plan takes it: on a return filed early it names the due date and says nothing is added before it; filed on or after the due date it gives what's owed with the penalty and interest charged. SLATE assesses at filing, so the CP14 is dated then (the IRS's own date is the Monday of the third week after posting: SLATE's simplification, said). (3) armCollection moves a letter that a save from before 2026-10-16 holds pending before its earliest lawful day (the due date plus its step's wait) to that day, once. (4) The guide, the tutorial's sentence and Papers' fine print say the bill comes at filing and the letters from the due date. (5) The tests that counted from an early filing are corrected: evidence-g17's journey files on the due date itself (where filing and the due date agree, so its 35th to 140th days after filing still hold); the federal lien test counts from the due date; scope-taxpapers' LT11 date and amount move to the IRS's lawful sequence, the title corrected and the audit's citation of it with it.

rows.goal: The passport's lifecycle: eligibility, application, fee and time, issue and term, renewal, loss and replacement, and what a missing or expired one does
rows.entry: src/engine/systems/documents.ts (passportTerms, passportRefusal, documents.apply_passport); src/engine/content/passportsabroad.ts (new: the offices' terms from abroad); src/ui/papers/Documents.tsx PassportPane; src/engine/content/guide/documents.ts
rows.preconditions: Each issuer's own rule for where the applicant is. A US citizen in the US renews by mail on Form DS-82 for $130 where the most recent passport was issued within the last 15 years, at 16 or older, valid for 10 years, never reported lost or stolen and undamaged (travel.state.gov 'Renew Your Passport by Mail', read 2026-10-16 through search; fee $130 in State's fee chart 'Updated October 2026', read through search 2026-10-16); otherwise Form DS-11, $130 and the $35 acceptance fee. A British national in the US applies from overseas: £116.50 online (gov.uk 'New fees for passport applications', published 18 March 2026, effective 8 April 2026, read 2026-10-16), and can't use the urgent Fast Track service ('You cannot use this service if you’re outside the UK', gov.uk/get-a-passport-urgently, read 2026-10-16). The other offices' rules from abroad as content/passports.ts's research of 2026-09-29 recorded them (`abroad`).
rows.reads: documents.apply_passport (documents.ts:314-331) charges every applicant the office's domestic fee (passportTerms, :411-414) and offers its expedite (:417-424), wherever they apply from. Every life is in New Haven, so a citizen of any other country applies from abroad: a London-born student pressing Renew It is charged the UK's £102 domestic fee and offered Renew It Faster, the UK's Fast Track (£192, 7 days), which isn't sold outside the UK; Papers shows the office's 'From abroad' text beside it, which says £116.50 (Documents.tsx:132) — the screen contradicts the charge. A US citizen renewing pays $165 (DS-11's $130 + $35) where DS-82 is $130. Loss: documents.report_lost (:333-349) cancels it; no replacement path besides applying again (correct: a lost passport is replaced by a new application). What a missing or expired one does: photoIdOf (a new bank), ssnRefusal (the SSA) — and nothing at the DMV for a non-citizen (tax.s8.idcard).
rows.decisions: Add the offices' terms from abroad (fee, currency, days, expedite, each assumption said) for the 14 non-US offices, from content/passports.ts's research of 2026-09-29 and the gov.uk pages read 2026-10-16; an applicant whose country isn't where they are applies on them; the US's renewal by mail on DS-82 for an eligible holder. Papers' A New One and Faster read the same terms the command charges, and Faster isn't drawn where the office sells none from abroad.

rows.goal: The state ID card's lifecycle (Connecticut's non-driver identification card) and the documents it requires
rows.entry: src/engine/systems/identity.ts (idCardRefusal, documents.apply_idcard); src/ui/looks/papers.tsx (the card's REAL ID line); src/engine/content/guide/documents.ts
rows.preconditions: Connecticut DMV's checklist (DI-3 Rev. 6-2026, 'REAL ID Document Identity Verification Checklist', read 2026-10-16 at portal.ct.gov): 'valid/unexpired, original documents'; two identity documents, one primary, a non-US-born applicant's primary being a foreign passport with its supporting documents ('F1 requires I-20 and I-94'), a Permanent Resident Card or an Employment Authorization Document (I-766), among others; the Social Security number or the SSA's ineligibility letter; two proofs of Connecticut residency; legal status checked through SAVE, ten business days or more; 'If you are not eligible for a verified REAL ID driver’s license or ID card, you will be issued a non-verified (Not for Federal Identification) driver’s license or ID card', and only US citizens and permanent residents are eligible for a verified one (portal.ct.gov, Drivers License Non-US Citizen Requirements, read 2026-10-16). The card costs $28 and is valid for seven years, and a new-issue card is processed at a DMV office and mailed within 20 business days (portal.ct.gov/dmv 'Get a non-driver ID', read 2026-10-16).
rows.reads: idCardRefusal (identity.ts:80-117) for somebody not a citizen asks lawful presence (an F-1 at school or a US permit), the number, and none held or pending; it never asks for a passport, so a London-born student at school who reported her passport lost (documents.report_lost, reachable on Papers) after her Social Security card came is issued the card with no primary identity document. documents.apply_idcard (:223-244) marks a non-citizen's Limited Term card realId: true (:238), and the look says 'It meets REAL ID.' (looks/papers.tsx:208), where Connecticut issues a non-citizen with temporary status a non-verified card. A citizen's card is in force at once (:242) and runs six years (content/identity.ts:59), where DMV mails it within 20 business days and gives seven: recorded, not changed (below).
rows.decisions: (1) A non-citizen at a US state's counter needs a primary identity document in force: their passport (with the I-20 and I-94 an F-1 student at school holds), or a US permit in force (OPT's EAD); without one the DMV refuses and says to renew or replace the passport on Papers. (2) A non-citizen's card isn't REAL ID: realId false, and its look says Not For Federal Identification. (3) The citizen's mailing (20 business days) and seven-year term: recorded as an uncertainty and a finding, not changed here (a citizen's card in force at once is what tests/evidence-g15-papers.test.ts's verified journey asserts; whether DMV hands a temporary credential a bank accepts meanwhile wasn't found).
